symptom: `describe microflow GenAICommons.Trace_GetModelSpanInput` (Evora): in a loop body a `split type` arm appends to $ModelInput and STOPS (no outgoing flow), the other arms meet and `break`; the description closes the split and prints `break;` after it, so every arm breaks — re-executed, the loop stops at the first ToolSpan instead of collecting all. Same class: MxModelReflection.IVK_RecalculateSize (seven case arms that each end the iteration fell into the shared `set $Size + 8`), TeamcenterToolkit.ExpandGRMInput_Create
cause: An activity with no outgoing flow ends the loop iteration in Studio Pro (a dead end, legal only in a loop body). The describer printed it as the last statement of its branch, and closing the branch falls into whatever the join leads to
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_show_helpers.go` (traverseFlowUntilMerge: `continue;` after a dead-end ActionActivity when `ctx.describeFallsOn`; joinGoesOn, fallsOnBefore; emitLoopBody resets it), `mdl/executor/exec_context.go` (describeFallsOn)
insight: Whether `continue;` is needed is not local: it depends on whether ANYTHING is printed after the branch closes, at any enclosing level up to the loop body (IVK's dead end sits in an `if` with no join, inside a `case` arm whose join goes on). Carried as a context flag set when a branch walk's stop merge goes on, inherited by nested walks, extended for a guard's THEN arm by the false continuation, reset per loop body. Emitting `continue;` everywhere would be equivalent but would change every loop whose last body activity is a dead end — the commonest loop there is. A ContinueEvent and a dead end compare equal in the invariant, so the rebuild differs only by that event. MDL cannot author a dead end; the fixture builds `continue` and strips the event. Guard `TestDescribeLoopDeadEndArm_*`
